predecessors.name: Gupta Empire
predecessors.text: Magadha, "the Magadha region of what is now Bihar"

successors.name: Kingdom of Kannauj
successors.text: Magadha widened under Adityasena: Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal

ledger.x: c. 490: Krishnagupta founds the Later Gupta line in Magadha. Infobox "Established: c. 490 CE"; the ruler list opens with Krishnagupta (c. 490-505). The land is the page's Magadha region.

c. 490: the Later Guptas are feudatories of the Imperial Guptas. "likely originally feudatories under the Imperial Guptas"; the dynasty is "Established c. 490 CE". gupta-empire draws all of Magadha to 554, so this is the relation that explains the double drawing 490-525. Direction: this state…

c. 575: Sharvavarman of the Maukharis invades Magadha and Mahasenagupta loses it. "Sharvavarman invaded Magadha 'circa 575 CE'"; "King of Magadha from 562 until his defeat in 575... Rivals then took Magadha".

c. 575: Mahasenagupta retreats to Malwa. "After losing Magadha, he retreated to Malwa, which he ruled as a reduced 'rump state'" and was "king of Malwa until his death in 601"; the Later Gupta page says Malwa was added under Mahasenagupta "but no date is given". The page does not say who held Malwa before. Review…

c. 597: Shankaragana takes Ujjain. "took Ujjain around 597 from Mahasenagupta"; a 597 CE inscription issued from Ujjain records a grant near Abhona. The Mahasenagupta page names Shankaragana as an adversary in Malwa. Review repair: the cells of the Ujjain disc inside the Mahishmati disc are the Kalachuris'…
605: Rajyavardhana defeats Devagupta and Malwa is lost.
c. 606: Magadha returns to the Later Guptas. "Harsha (c. 606-647 CE) restored Later Gupta rule in Magadha". Counterpart changed from nobody to the Maukharis, who took Magadha in 575: the…
c. 606: the restored Later Guptas are Harsha's vassals. "they ruled as Harsha's vassals"; "Madhavagupta was made the Kannauj vassal of Magadha after the war".…

c. 655: Adityasena widens the kingdom. "Under Adityasena, the kingdom reached from the Himalayan foothills to Chhota Nagpur, and from the Gomati River to the Bay of Bengal"; his reign is c. 655-680. The page does not date the widening or name who held the land. Review repair: region reduced to the land beyond Magadha…

c. 750: Yashovarman of Kannauj defeats Jivitagupta II. "Jivitagupta II appears to have been defeated by Yashovarman of Kannauj 'circa 750 CE'. The details are recorded in the Gaudavaho." Infobox "Disestablished: c. 750 CE".

wars.name: Later Gupta wars with the Maukharis
wars.outcome: Kumaragupta defeats Isanavarman in 554; Damodaragupta is pushed back into Magadha c.

wars.name: Mahasenagupta's war with Susthitavarman of Kamarupa
Rajyavardhana's defeat of Devagupta
wars.outcome: Rajyavardhana defeated Devagupta, Mahasenagupta's son in Malwa, and Madhavagupta was made a vassal over Magadha.

wars.name: Devagupta against the Chalukyas
wars.outcome: An encounter "on or around 696 CE" under Devagupta ended in a Later Gupta defeat.

certainty.note: No border is given for any year; the extent is a region by name (Magadha, Malwa) and, for Adityasena, the page's description from the Himalayan foothills to Chhota Nagpur.
